newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies following a sharp decline on Monday, dealers said.

"The market is very nervous and we saw today large conversions of foreign currency into shekels. On Monday investors panicked and the shekel declined. People were over-reacting and today everybody is less worried," a dealer said.
"If the Washington summit succeeds the market will return to behaving normally," he said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton called for a two-day summit to defuse tensions between Israelis and Palesinians. Five days of clashes that killed 72 people erupted after Israel opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1920 against 3.2200 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5668 shekels against 3.5958 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8723 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8905 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0941 shekels per mark against 2.1093 on Monday.
The Bank of Israel set the representative rate early on Monday due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth and will do so throughout the week.
In the afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1850 shekels.
